Sound Credit Union Selects Temenos SaaS to Modernize Collections Operations
summary:
Temenos, a global leader in banking technology, today announced that Sound Credit Union (Sound), one of Washington State’s largest credit unions, has selected Temenos Collections delivered as Temenos SaaS to modernize its collections operations.
Sound provides financial products and services to consumers and businesses across Washington state and serves more than 183,000 members through 26 full-service branch locations. The credit union selected Temenos following a comprehensive evaluation of its operations and supporting technology, with the goal of improving efficiency, data accuracy, collector productivity and service to members.
With Temenos Collections on SaaS, Sound gains a modern, cloud-based platform with real-time integration to its core system, helping teams view multiple accounts, improve data visibility and adopt software updates more efficiently. The solution also supports flexible customization, improved note tracking, automated data capture, simplified pay processes, and better document and workflow management.
Stephanie Mabry, VP of Loss Management & Loan Servicing, Sound Credit Union, commented: “At Sound, we are committed to giving our teams the tools they need to work efficiently while delivering high-quality service to our members. Temenos provides the modern collections capabilities, real-time core integration and flexibility we need to improve productivity, strengthen data accuracy and support a more member-centric collections experience.”
Brian DuVal, President, North America, Temenos, said: “Credit unions are looking for modern, scalable technology that helps them operate more efficiently while continuing to put members first. We are proud to support Sound as it moves collections to Temenos SaaS. The US is a strategic growth market for Temenos, and we continue to invest in strengthening our regional presence and innovation to meet the evolving needs of US banks and credit unions.”

title: FIS AML Investigations Agent Now Commercially Available to Help Banks Tackle the Scale and Cost of Financial Crime Compliance
summary:
FIS®  today announced that the FIS AML Investigations Agent that was jointly announced in May 2026 with Anthropic, is now commercially available to any U.S.-based bank, including those that are not FIS clients today. This is the first solution of its kind from a provider that already operates the core banking, payments and data infrastructure financial crime investigations depend on, with built-in controls that keep analysts in command of every decision.
FIS built the agent with support from Anthropic and design partner Amalgamated Bank. The agent is now being deployed at Amalgamated.
The scale of the challenge is significant. U.S. financial institutions spend an estimated $35 to $40 billion a year on anti-money laundering operations (LexisNexis, 2023), yet analysts devote 40 to 60 percent of investigation time to assembling data before analysis can begin (AnChain.AI, 2025). Industry false-positive rates run between 90 and 95 percent (Datos Insights, 2023). Alert volumes keep climbing. The gap is not analytical capacity - it is the manual evidence assembly that consumes it.
Based on Amalgamated’s analysis of its investigation workflows combined with the AML Investigations Agent’s expected abilities, the agent is projected to reduce Level 1 alert review time by more than 90 percent, Level 2 case investigation time by approximately 98 percent, and SAR narrative preparation time by more than 80 percent - freeing investigators to redirect capacity from data assembly to complex cases that require greater judgment.
The agent applies customer-specific context to every investigation rather than treating all alerts the same. It maps the customer’s type, historical activity and expected behavior against the alert before assembling evidence, so the resulting summary is already calibrated to what is and is not normal for that customer. A seasonal spike in cash deposits looks different from deposits deliberately kept just under federal reporting thresholds. A routine international transfer looks different from an unexplained cross-border wire to a high-risk jurisdiction. The agent identifies those distinctions and explains the rationale to the analyst.
The agent is built on FIS’ Trust Assured framework, which embeds governance, compliance and responsible AI into every FIS product. Every output links to the specific record, document or check image it came from. Every recommendation, the reasoning behind it and the analyst's final decision are logged in a complete audit trail, so investigation outcomes are explainable and ready for internal audit or regulatory examination. Each institution's risk logic, thresholds and investigation procedures remain isolated through the FIS Control Plane, FIS's governance layer for managing agent access, controls and institution-specific configurations. The agent is designed to augment, not replace, the monitoring platforms and case management systems a bank already runs, and natively integrates with FIS Horizon and FIS Systematics, two of FIS core banking platforms, with FIS IBS planned next on the product roadmap.
“Investigations don’t slow down because analysts lack judgment. They slow down because evidence is scattered across systems and every alert gets treated the same,” said Stan Szwalbenest, Head of Enterprise Fraud and Financial Crimes, FIS. “By bringing together the core, payments and data these investigations rely on, FIS gives analysts a head start while keeping them in control of every decision.”
“AML investigations require comprehensive evidence and experienced judgment. The FIS AML Investigations Agent can reduce time spent gathering information and preparing documentation, allowing investigators to focus on complex cases and critical decisions. Each recommendation has a clear audit trail, while the investigator remains accountable for the final determination. In regulated environments, AI must strengthen human expertise while preserving trust and governance,” said Sean Searby, Chief Information & Operations Officer, Amalgamated Bank.
FIS developed and owns the AML Investigations Agent, built with support from an Anthropic team that embedded with FIS product and compliance teams, drawing on FIS’ financial-institution relationships, regulatory expertise and transaction-data infrastructure. The collaboration also produced the evaluation frameworks and engineering practices FIS will use to build and scale additional agents on the same governed platform. The agent runs in FIS’ private cloud and uses Anthropic’s Claude models.

Iberdrola, BBVA and Santander Deliver the First Syndicated Financing Managed Entirely on Blockchain
summary:
Iberdrola, BBVA and Santander arranged a €150 million corporate syndicated financing facility, managed entirely using distributed ledger technology (DLT), commonly known as blockchain. The transaction marks a milestone for the financial market as the first live syndicated loan whose entire lifecycle, from execution and disbursement through to the management of interest, waivers, repayments, assignments and maturity, is administered using this technology. The transaction aligns with Iberdrola’s digital transformation strategy, which places innovation, data and emerging technologies at the heart of its efforts to drive efficiency and streamline financial and treasury processes. Gómez-Acebo & Pombo acted as legal advisers on the transaction.
The digital infrastructure enables participating institutions to share and maintain a single, synchronised and immutable record of information, replacing reconciliation processes between separate databases with a single shared source of information. This technology improves transaction traceability, reduces the risk of operational errors and facilitates more efficient management of syndicated financing, enabling the various participants to interact in an orderly manner under the operational control of the agent bank appointed for the financing.
Throughout the life of the loan, the platform manages the main contractual events in a coordinated manner, including the calculation and notification of interest, payments of principal and fees, early repayments, monitoring compliance with agreed financial covenants and information undertakings, the processing of certain contractual consents, and transfers of participations between lending institutions. All these events are recorded on the DLT infrastructure and are visible in real time to authorised participants.
The application of distributed ledger technology to the syndicated loan market makes it possible to simplify the management of financing lifecycles, reduce operating costs, improve coordination between institutions and increase the efficiency of one of the most important segments of corporate financing. It may also help increase market liquidity and facilitate access to this type of financing for mid-sized companies by simplifying processes that have traditionally limited their participation in these transactions.
The transaction was managed through the platform developed by ioBuilders with the support of BBVA and Santander to digitalise the management of syndicated financing. Following this first transaction, the institutions will work on progressively onboarding new participants and expanding the platform’s functionalities, with the aim of moving towards a shared infrastructure for the syndicated loan market. The goal is to harness the potential of distributed ledger technology to modernise one of the most important markets in corporate finance, traditionally characterised by a high administrative burden and intensive coordination among multiple participants, including the agent bank, lending banks and the client.
Rob Kay, Global Head of Investment Grade and Emerging Markets Debt at Santander CIB, said: “Innovation is part of Santander’s DNA. This transaction represents an important step forward in the evolution of syndicated financing, demonstrating how DLT-based technologies can bring greater efficiency, transparency and traceability to complex financial processes. It also highlights how digital assets are already generating tangible value for the business and contributing to the transformation of financial markets. At the same time, it lays the foundations for an industry collaboration model with the potential to redefine different aspects of corporate financing.”
Alberto Falco, Head of Portfolio Monitoring and Innovation at BBVA CIB, said: “This transaction reflects BBVA’s commitment to the digitalisation of financial markets. Blockchain technology enables a particularly significant transformational leap in syndicated loans, a product that has traditionally seen limited digitalisation and has been accessible to very few clients. By combining the advantages of DLT as an immutable record with the programmability of smart contracts to automate operational processes, our ambition is for this platform to become a meeting point that other institutions can join to help drive the syndicated loan market.”
“The adoption of blockchain technology in financial environments is increasingly becoming a reality thanks to the benefits it provides. With this transaction, we demonstrate that these advantages can also be extended to a live syndicated loan and its end-to-end management, with full legal validity and based on a single source of information shared by all parties. It is also worth highlighting that the technology underpinning this platform opens the door to more efficient management of financial institutions’ balance sheets, enabling new strategies for loan mobilisation in the secondary market,” said Carlos Matilla, CEO of ioBuilders.

content: Iberdrola, BBVA and Santander have arranged a corporate syndicated financing facility managed entirely using blockchain technology. title: Industry and Government Back CFIT Financial Inclusion Coalition
summary:
After the Economic Secretary to the Treasury’s welcomed CFIT’s Financial Inclusion Coalition at the Fintech as a Force for Good conference in London last week, CFIT is today announcing that several major UK banks – including Natwest, Nationwide and HSBC UK - will participate in the Coalition, highlighting Government and industry support for the initiative to develop a new Supported Payments framework.
The announcement demonstrates the growing momentum behind the coalition, bringing together Government, major financial institutions, regulators, technology providers, the Third Sector and people with lived experience around a shared ambition to tackle a longstanding systemic challenge in the UK. 
A significant number of people need help from someone they trust to manage everyday payments, including people with learning disabilities and others who may need support while retaining the ability to make their own financial decisions. Current banking arrangements do not adequately support this need. As a result, people and their supporters can be pushed towards informal and potentially unsafe workarounds, including sharing cards, PINs or online banking credentials.
The framework will address the gap between managing finances entirely independently and formal arrangements such as Power of Attorney or deputyship. The aim is to increase independence and control while providing appropriate safeguards for customers, trusted third parties, and financial services providers. 
From Project Nemo to practical delivery
The Financial Inclusion Coalition builds on more than two years of work led by Project Nemo, which grew from a grassroots initiative focused on disability inclusion into a wider crosssector movement bringing together banks, fintechs, charities, policymakers, regulators and, critically, people with lived experience.
In a major research publication, led by Nationwide, Project Nemo helped identify a significant gap in the way financial services support people who need assistance managing their money. For many, the current options can fall between managing finances entirely independently, relying on informal and potentially risky arrangements such as sharing passwords or PINs, or moving to formal legal mechanisms such as Power of Attorney or deputyship.
This work helped build wider recognition of the need for change. HM Treasury’s Financial Inclusion Strategy recognised Project Nemo’s work identifying barriers faced by disabled consumers, with Government subsequently providing funding to CFIT to take the work forward. The launch of CFIT’s Financial Inclusion Coalition with Project Nemo at Money20/20 Europe marked the next stage in that journey: moving from identifying the problem and mobilising the industry towards developing, testing and ultimately implementing a practical solution.
The Coalition is now developing a Supported Payments framework, bringing together financial institutions, technology providers, Government, regulators, the Third Sector and people with lived experience. The aim is to establish how trusted third-party support could work safely in practice – giving people appropriate help with everyday payments while allowing them to retain as much independence, choice and control as possible. 
That progression is important to the wider CFIT story: Project Nemo helped surface the challenge and build the case for action; Government recognised the issue and provided support; CFIT is now bringing the ecosystem together to turn that momentum into a practical, scalable solution.
From industry mobilisation to practical delivery
Throughout the remainder of 2026, Coalition participants will undertake a series of focused sprints to develop a Trust & Governance Framework and test key elements of the Supported Payments model, including digital identity verification and approaches to assessing a customer’s ability to use the service. 
Crucially, people with lived experience will be directly involved in designing and testing the proposed customer journey. 
This work will culminate in an Interim Report later this year, setting out the Coalition’s initial findings and Trust & Governance Framework, and informing the next phase of the programme which will focus on building and testing a Minimum Viable Product for Supported Payments.
Anna Wallace, CEO of CFIT, said: “For too many people, getting help to manage their money still means giving up more control than they should have to. Tackling that challenge requires coordinated action across the industry. CFIT is here to do exactly that: marshal the expertise, commitment and resources needed to move beyond recognising the problem to developing and testing practical solutions that deliver meaningful change.”

title: Smarsh Taps Former ACI Worldwide Executive Alessandro Silva as Chief Growth Officer to Drive Its Next Phase of Global Expansion
summary:
Smarsh, the global leader in communications data and intelligence, today announced the appointment of Alessandro Silva as Chief Growth Officer. In this newly created role, Silva will unite Smarsh’s Enterprise, Corporate, Public Sector, and Global Channel business units under one commercial strategy, accelerating execution, and driving the company’s next phase of international growth.
The move comes as organizations worldwide face rising volumes of digital communications, new forms of AI-driven collaboration, and increasingly complex regulation. A unified go-to-market organization will speed decision-making, deliver a more consistent customer experience, and still adapt to the needs of different industries, regions, and regulatory environments.
"Smarsh has an exceptional foundation for global growth: trusted technology, talented people, and a customer base that includes 80% of the world's top global banks," said Kim Crawford Goodman, CEO of Smarsh. "Alessandro brings the global perspective and proven leadership we need to turn that opportunity into sustained growth."
Silva joins from ACI Worldwide, where as Chief Revenue Officer he led the global commercial organization, including sales effectiveness, go-to-market strategy, and customer success. He previously held senior sales and general management roles at Western Union, GE Capital, and The Carlyle Group.
"Growth may be my mandate, but it is a shared mission, and every team across Smarsh has a role in achieving it," said Silva. "My focus is turning our strengths into a connected commercial strategy that helps us serve customers more effectively and scale with greater speed and consistency."
Momentum behind the appointment
Silva joins as Smarsh sets the pace for AI innovation in communications data and intelligence. In 2026, Smarsh launched Discovery Agent, its MCP Server, AskSmarsh AI, and MySearch Agent, and extended capture to Claude Enterprise, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Workspace so regulated firms can adopt AI with confidence. The company was also named to the Inc. 5000 for the 19th straight year, a Leader in the 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for the ninth consecutive year, and winner of a 2026 Business Intelligence Group AI Excellence Award for Fraud Detection and Prevention.
